previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Ms. ___ was admitted with worsening shortness of breath, cough with reddish-brown sputum, and significant bilateral lower extremity edema, following non-compliance with her furosemide. She has a complex history including COPD, asthma, prior lung and tracheal cancer, atrial fibrillation, and chronic kidney disease. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic systolic and diastolic heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (40-45%), likely exacerbated by fluid overload, COPD flare, and uncontrolled atrial fibrillation. She was treated with IV diuresis, transitioned to torsemide, and optimized heart failure medications including switching from carvedilol to metoprolol. Her COPD exacerbation was managed with antibiotics, systemic steroids, and addition of budesonide nebulizers. Due to a CHADS2 score of 2, she was started on warfarin for stroke prevention. Her renal function fluctuated but stabilized, attributed to volume status and medications. She improved clinically, lost weight, and was discharged home with home health, a steroid taper, and close follow-up plans.
